# Task P0-03: Persistence with EF Core and SQLite

**Phase:** 0 · **Depends on:** P0-01 · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
A SQLite database (WAL mode) managed by EF Core 10 with checked-in migrations, created and migrated automatically at startup, holding the first two tables from the data model: `setting` and `job`. A settings repository gives later tasks a typed key/value store.

## Deliverables
All new code under `src/Compilarr.Core/Persistence/` (namespace `Compilarr.Core.Persistence`):
- `EntityBase` (abstract): `long Id`, `DateTime CreatedAt`, `DateTime UpdatedAt` (UTC).
- `Setting : EntityBase` — `string Key` (unique index), `string Value` (JSON text). Table `setting`.
- `Job : EntityBase` — `string Name` (unique index), `TimeSpan? Interval`, `DateTime? LastRunAt`, `DateTime? NextRunAt`, `string? LastResult`. Table `job`. (P0-06 fills it; this task only creates it.)
- `CompilarrDbContext` — `DbSet<Setting> Settings`, `DbSet<Job> Jobs`; `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()` from `EFCore.NamingConventions` so columns are `created_at`, `last_run_at` …; explicit `ToTable("setting")` / `ToTable("job")`. Overrides `SaveChanges`/`SaveChangesAsync` to stamp `CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt` from an injected `TimeProvider` (`GetUtcNow().UtcDateTime`). No lazy loading.
- `DesignTimeDbContextFactory : IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<CompilarrDbContext>` (uses `Data Source=design.db`) so `dotnet ef` works with Core as both project and startup project.
- `Migrations/` — one migration named `InitialCreate`, generated with the local `dotnet-ef` tool, never hand-written.
- `DatabaseMigrator` — `Task MigrateAsync(CancellationToken)`: applies pending migrations, then executes `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;` and logs the resulting mode. `DatabaseMigrationHostedService : IHostedService` calls it in `StartAsync` (so the database is ready before the server accepts requests).
- `ISettingsRepository` / `SettingsRepository` — `Task<T?> GetAsync<T>(string key, CancellationToken ct)`, `Task SetAsync<T>(string key, T value, CancellationToken ct)` (upsert; `System.Text.Json` with web defaults), `Task<bool> DeleteAsync(string key, CancellationToken ct)`.
- In `src/Compilarr.Core/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`: `AddCompilarrPersistence(this IServiceCollection services, string connectionString)` registering the context (`UseSqlite(connectionString)`), `TimeProvider.System` via `TryAddSingleton`, the repository (scoped), the migrator and the hosted service. Keep the existing `AddCompilarrCore()`. **Do not edit `Program.cs`** — the orchestrator wires it after P0-02 lands.
- `.config/dotnet-tools.json` — local tool manifest with `dotnet-ef` 10.0.12 (`dotnet new tool-manifest`, `dotnet tool install dotnet-ef --version 10.0.12`).

## Allowed paths
- `src/Compilarr.Core/Persistence/**`, `src/Compilarr.Core/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`, `src/Compilarr.Core/Compilarr.Core.csproj`
- `.config/dotnet-tools.json`
- `Directory.Packages.props` (add only the packages listed below)
- `tests/Compilarr.Core.Tests/**`

## Context to read first
- `docs/build/CODING_STANDARDS.md` (Persistence, Tests)
- `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.4 (rows `setting` and `job`; every table has `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`)
- `src/Compilarr.Core/Compilarr.Core.csproj`, `Directory.Packages.props`

## Constraints
- Package versions (already resolved; do not look them up): `EFCore.NamingConventions` 10.0.1, `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions` 10.0.12, `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing` 10.10.0 (tests only). EF Core Sqlite/Design 10.0.12 are already in `Directory.Packages.props`.
- Generate the migration with: `dotnet tool restore` then `dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate --project src/Compilarr.Core --startup-project src/Compilarr.Core --output-dir Persistence/Migrations`. Delete any `design.db` it leaves behind.
- The generated migration files are exempt from analyzers: add a new `src/Compilarr.Core/Persistence/Migrations/.editorconfig` with `[*.cs]` → `generated_code = true` if the build warns about them.
- Tests use a real SQLite file in a per-test temp directory (WAL needs a file); delete it afterwards (call `SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools()` first on Windows). Use `FakeTimeProvider` for timestamps.

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)
1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` → `Build succeeded.` with 0 warnings; `dotnet test` → all pass.
2. Test: `DatabaseMigrator.MigrateAsync` on a new file creates it; `PRAGMA journal_mode` returns `wal`; tables `setting` and `job` exist with snake_case columns (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_run_at`); `__EFMigrationsHistory` lists `InitialCreate`.
3. Test: running the migrator twice is a no-op (no exception, one history row).
4. Test: `SetAsync("ui.theme", new { Mode = "dark" })` then `GetAsync<…>` round-trips through a **new** context; a second `SetAsync` on the same key updates the row (still one row) and changes `UpdatedAt` but not `CreatedAt`; `DeleteAsync` removes it; `GetAsync` of a missing key returns `default`.
5. Test: inserting two `Job` rows with the same `Name` fails with `DbUpdateException`.
6. `dotnet ef migrations list --project src/Compilarr.Core --startup-project src/Compilarr.Core` shows `InitialCreate` (paste the line).

## Out of scope
- Wiring into `Program.cs`; any other table; repositories beyond settings; Quartz (P0-06).
